leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Apply TypeScript interfaces to define a User type with properties for authentication data.
Implement React state hooks to store and update authentication status and user information.
Utilize conditional rendering to display different UI components based on the user's login state.
Construct a login form component with controlled input fields for username and password.
Handle form submission events to process user credentials and trigger authentication logic.
Execute mock API calls to simulate user login and logout operations.
Control application routing by conditionally redirecting users based on their authentication status.
Define context providers to make authentication state available across multiple components.
Invoke context hooks to access authentication functions and data within child components.
Store authentication tokens in the browser's localStorage to persist user sessions.
Retrieve stored authentication data on application initialization to restore the user's session.
Modify state and UI elements in response to successful login or logout actions.
